column1: # aliases.tsv (harbor#950) — every alias the naming lint confines or rejects, and where it may appear.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Technical terms are canonical; nautical and legacy words survive only as
# aliases on the surfaces listed here (standards/naming.md §1.3). It replaces the reserved
# nautical layer words of CONTRACTS/naming.md. Each row is one word or kebab phrase, matched
# against the words of a name in any position (D-38), so an alias is found inside
#   codename      a brand or repo name: allowed only on the surfaces listed, never expires
#   legacy        a replaced word: allowed only in the glossary, this file, dated records and old
#                 memory prose (none of them a name surface), removed on remove_by (default
#                 2027-01-31). From remove_by minus 14 days it is a finding (name.alias-expired).
#   banned        never in a name; glossary only (bare "golden", "self-healing", "signed")
#   abbreviation  an abbreviation that is NOT registered: spell out the word in `term` (D-18).
#                 Registered abbreviations are terms.tsv rows of class abbreviation.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> term <TAB> kind <TAB> surfaces <TAB> remove_by <TAB> note
#   id        the alias, lowercase kebab; never equal to a term id (SKOS: labels are disjoint)
#   term      the terms.tsv id to use instead (an abbreviation's spelled-out word; - for banned)
#   surfaces  where the alias is allowed, comma-separated; - for nowhere
